 Big Emirates NBA Cup 2026 nights for Giannis Antetokounmpo and Alperen Sengun
 By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net 
 Nine games took place on Friday, counting toward both the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season and the Emirates NBA Cup 2026. The slate included a fourth-quarter push by the Miami Heat , who pulled away for a 133–121 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers at Kaseya Center.
 Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo shared a game-high 37 points. The Greek point forward shot 15-for-20 from the floor alongside nine rebounds, two assists, and one block. Italian Simone Fontecchio saw 7:26 of floor time, Serbian Nikola Jovic stayed on the bench, and Swedish guard Pelle Larsson sat out with an illness. For the Cavs , Croatian Mario Hezonja got four points.
 At Toyota Center, the Houston Rockets edged out the Utah Jazz 125–118 behind Alperen Sengun, who neared his career-high with 43 points and grabbed 12 boards in a monster double-double.  “Huge. I mean, dominant. He fouled some guys out. They were blitzing him, and he was finding all the right guys and picked them apart so well that they stopped going after him, and he had the matchups that he liked, and we liked,” head coach Ime Udoka praised his starting center during the postgame press conference. “Obviously won the game for us with his scoring and kind of keeping us floating in the lows, and then took over toward the end.” 
 Serbian Bogdan Bogdanovic added 11 points off the bench for Houston. On the wrong end, Ukrainian Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk went scoreless in seven minutes.
 Meanwhile, the San Antonio Spurs secured an 11th consecutive win, blowing out the shorthanded Golden State Warriors 123–85 at Frost Bank Center. French superstar Victor Wembanyama was needed for just under 21 minutes, during which he tallied 12 points, 12 rebounds, six assists, two blocks, and one steal. For the visitors, Dutch Malevy Leons logged five points.
 Franz Wagner powers Orlando
 Over at Kia Center, German Franz Wagner carried the Orlando Magic to a 107–99 triumph against the Milwaukee Bucks . He finished one rebound shy of a triple-double with 35 points, 12 assists, and nine boards.  “Not an easy one with the travel that we had. It’s not an excuse, but I think we can play a little better. But overall, I liked our energy, our effort, and our talk throughout the game,” mentioned the 25-year-old forward during his postgame press conference, referencing a recently concluded four-game road trip.
 Fellow German Tristan da Silva returned from a left calf strain and put up 12 points as a starter. Off the bench, Georgian Goga Bitadze genarated 12 more points and Montenegrin Nikola Vucevic had two. For Milwaukee, French Ousmane Dieng started but played just 4:47 without scoring, and Italian Nate Ament netted nine points, but Lithuanian Kasparas Jakucionis and Serbian Bogoljub Markovic never checked in.
 In a close contest at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, Croatian starter Ivica Zubac recorded 12 points and 13 rebounds as the Indiana Pacers held off the New York Knicks , 106–104. Starting for the defending champions, British OG Anunoby finished with 11 points, with French teammates Pacome Dadiet and Mohamed Diawara ranging from 69 seconds to a DNP.
 At United Center, the Chicago Bulls outlasted the Atlanta Hawks 125–117 in overtime after blowing an 18-point lead. Josh Giddey paved the way with a triple-double, while Lithuanian Matas Buzelis contributed 11 points, and French reserve Noa Essengue supplied five.
 Coached by Finn Tuomas Iisalo, the Memphis Grizzlies routed the New Orleans Pelicans 142–111 at Smoothie King Center. “Super proud of our performance,” noted 44-year-old Iisalo. European involvement on the floor was brief, with Croatian Karlo Matkovic sinking one free throw for the Pels.
